source.episode_title: God Answered Snakebite With a Snake on a Pole
source.anchor_kjv: And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
source.thread: The cure was lifted up where all could see
source.spoken_script: Snakes were killing my people. God's cure? A snake. I am Moses. My people spoke against God. He sent snakes. Many died. They cried, "We have sinned". I prayed. God did not take the snakes away. He said: make a snake, set it on a pole. I made one of brass, and lifted it up. Anyone bitten who looked at it, lived. The cure looked like the thing that was killing them. I lived long before Jesus, God's Son. But He said: "as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up". Lifted up: He meant Himself, on a cross. A later writer, Paul, said that on the cross God "made him to be sin for us". The bitten looked at a snake, and lived. Believe in Jesus, lifted up on the cross, and live.

platforms.description:
Numbers 21:8-9: snakes were killing Israel, and God did not take the snakes away. He told Moses to make a serpent of brass and set it on a pole, and whoever looked at it lived. Jesus pointed back to this scene in John 3:14, and said the Son of man must be lifted up the same way.

"And the LORD said unto Moses, Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live. And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived." (Numbers 21:8-9, KJV)

The bitten looked at a snake, and lived. Believe in Jesus, lifted up on the cross, and live.

redteam:
VERDICT: PASS
- Anchor quote: matches Numbers 21:8-9 KJV. No change.
- Title: the hook is true to the text (God told Moses to set a brass serpent on a pole, Num 21:8-9). Not clickbait.
- Doctrine: John 3:14 link is Jesus's own words, so the metadata does not invent the typology. "Believe in Jesus" matches John 3:15.
- "God did not take the snakes away" is an inference from the text (the people asked for it, Num 21:7, and God gave a remedy instead). Reasonable, and not stated as a verse.
- Platform: TikTok/Instagram hooks come first. Fine.
